correctness.rationale: The cited v1 stage equations and coefficients, not merely the stability polynomials, give the two forcing samples. On appending time as a component with derivative 1, their offsets are α/(α−e)−1 and that offset plus β/(4ω). The two sample weights agree because m₂ times the first-stage forcing coefficient equals the second-stage forcing coefficient before the common output factor. From the published polynomial order conditions with q=eT₂(ω), preconsistency gives δ=(1−e)/(1+q/e), first order gives δβω=1−q, and the second-order coefficient equation is δβ²/8+eβω=(1+q)/2. Inserting ω²=(1+q/e)/2 yields 3q²+2eq+1−6e=0. The radical root tending to 1 yields positive α,β,ω in the stated neighborhood. The constant and linear forcing moments cancel the t_n² and t_n defect terms; the remaining cubic term has the stated Laurent expansion, independently expanded exactly. With exact starts the final error is h³E times Σ_{j=1}^{N−1}(1−q^j)/(1−q), so the three limits follow from N(1−q) tending to infinity, a positive constant, or zero. In the last case the geometric sums are uniformly asymptotic to j; in the critical case the limit is positive because x−1+e⁻ˣ>0 for x>0. Any sequence for which ε/h fails to diverge has a bounded subsequence, then a further subsequence with a finite limit; both the zero and positive finite cases preclude zero final error. This checks necessity for arbitrary allowed mesh sequences, not just the examples in the frozen checker.
residual_risks: Only the specified two-stage branch, exact arithmetic, exact starts and the polynomial forcing test are classified. There is no assertion of sufficiency for general nonautonomous equations under the same scale condition or about higher-stage schemes.

value.rationale: A single cubic exact solution with no startup error establishes a sharp practical obstruction to tuning damping with the mesh. It explains what the fixed-damping order and stability results cannot detect: diverging stage times and accumulated forcing errors yield a finite nonzero critical limit and divergence below threshold. This is stronger than numerically displaying an unstable step or checking a single damping value.
residual_risks: The theorem diagnoses this construction and forcing test, not all stabilized schemes, software behavior or finite-precision robustness.
